Google SWE Intern Interview Experience (Round 1) – Tree DP + AI Fluency
Had my Round 1 interview for the Google SWE Intern position today, so I thought I'd share my experience in case it helps others preparing.

The interview lasted around **1 hour** and consisted of one coding problem with a follow-up, followed by a few AI fluency questions.

### Question 1

You are given a **weighted binary tree**, where each edge has a positive integer weight. Your task is to remove a set of edges such that every leaf node becomes disconnected from the root. Removing an edge incurs a cost equal to its weight. Find the minimum total cost required to disconnect all leaf nodes from the root.

I proposed a **postorder traversal** solution where each subtree computes the minimum cost required to disconnect all leaves in that subtree. The interviewer was happy with the approach, and we discussed the recurrence and complexity.

### Follow-up

The interviewer then generalized the problem:

> How would you solve the same problem if the tree were an **N-ary tree** instead of a binary tree?

The core idea remained the same, but instead of handling two children, the solution had to work for an arbitrary number of children. I reached the final approach with a couple of hints from the interviewer.

### AI Fluency

The last few minutes were dedicated to AI-related questions (around 3–4 of them). The interviewer asked me questions like how do I use AI in my regular workflow and do I give the AI complete ownership of my project, how I manage to use AI for tasks like debugging and stuff like this.

Congratulations on getting interview call at Google. Almost 2 and half years back I also got a call from Google after APAC and appeared Google interview at Bangalore office. I went through 4 rounds of interview and I am sharing my experience in details below.

During all of my rounds, each of the interviewers was from Google Mountain View office. They were smart, friendly and made the interviews seem very interesting. Each round lasted for about 1 hour and the problems were open ended which force applicant to think thoroughly and approach from different angles. I enjoyed the interview and hence I remember every bit of it.

* Given a file of size 1TB in a disc, problem was to select a small sample from the file. Assuming File has N records, a solution should be able to choose K records effectively.
* Our discussion started with simple algorithms to take a sample of size K from an array of size N and gradually extended to OS concepts regarding file storage in hard-disks.
* I was asked to compare the time complexities/ space complexities/ drawbacks and advantages of each algorithm over other proposed by me.

title: Design a High-Traffic Website
reported: Design a website that can handle very high traffic: distributed databases, caching, session management, scaling up vs out, REST.

sources.passage:
mped to a system design problem. How would you design a web site which can handle high traffic? The problem was very vague and we had a lot of discussions about distributed databases, caching, session management, scale up/out, RESTFUL designs etc.

****Round 3****

* I found 4th round bit difficult, but very interesting. We had lot of arguments and discussions.
* Given a master-slave architecture to store logs of a google system, where each slave has terabytes of logs stored in a file. Each file is a CSV formatted file where each row has data in [timestamp, log-data] format. Now design a solution where the master will print all the logs from all the slaves in sorted format with respect to the timestamp. Additional, The log file in the slave might not be sorted. To be clear, for a Master-Slave architecture with 2 slaves, if slave 1 has 10M logs and slave 2 has 20M logs. Then master should be able to print all the 30M logs in sorted format.
* We discussed different approach, but he didn’t seem satisfied with any of the approach. Also, he asked me to code my proposed solution. I was not convinced with myself after this round.

I got the result after a month and couldn’t get through. However, I’m glad that I have this wonderful experience.

Best of luck with your interviews. :)

Google L5 Interview Experience | Onsite Bangalore 2025
I didn't have a phone screen cause this is my second onsite. Round 1 dsa and Googleyness were online and the other 3 were onsite at their bangalore office.

Round 1
Graph problem - Given network of routers where some are defective, a source and a destination, check if a broadcast and shut down msg will reach destination. 

Round 2
1. Binary search - first bad commit
Follow up - what if the size is too large and the l,r pointers cause integer overflow
2. Dp - given a mapping of digits to alphabets (1:a, 26:z) and a string of digits, return the number of possible interpretations.

Round 3
1. Logger rate limiter
2. Dont log the msg if repeated more than once in a 10s window.

title: Employee Cab Transport System
reported: Design an end-to-end system for Google's employee cab service optimising cab allocation, routing and scheduling to cut wait and travel time at scale.

sources.passage:
Google system design rounds
Recently, I went through a Google system design interview where I was asked to design an end-to-end system for Google’s employee cab transportation service. The goal was to optimize cab allocation, routing, and scheduling in order to improve efficiency, reduce wait and travel time, and enhance the overall employee experience at scale.”
